info.title: WtF API
info.description:
Version 1 of the API, served under /api/v1. Within a version the API only
grows (new routes, optional fields, fields in answers); every answer names
the current revision in the `API-Revision` header. A breaking change would
become /api/v2, served next to /api/v1 for a while. A request for a
version the server doesn't serve gets an `unsupported-api-version`
problem that lists the versions it does serve (`supported`). The
refactors of 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02 changed /api/v1 in place, and its
revision started again at 1 (WTFD.md, "Versions").

Where to Find: a register of the things you own and where they are.
Every endpoint calls one database function; see API.md for the semantics
and WTFD.md for the HTTP conventions. One server is one installation.

- A class has attributes, its own and those it inherits. An item's and a
  stock row's values are a JSON object by attribute name (`values`), with
  the names of those that follow the class's default (`defaulted`).
- Everything has UUIDs as ids; attributes are named.
- Every account has a role (ACCOUNTS.md): a `viewer` reads everything
  but the accounts; a `user` also changes items and stock rows (with
  their values and files); an `admin` also sets up locations and classes
  with their attributes, imports and exports model files, and manages
  accounts. A request the role doesn't allow gets 403.
- A field the server needs is required in a request body, even if as
  null; nothing is assumed.
- Lists are paged by key: a page answers `more` and, when there is more,
  `next`, the `after` of the next page. They give no total.
- Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`).
- `GET /classes` and `GET /locations` support `ETag` / `If-None-Match`.
- POST /login sets the session cookie `wtf_session` (HttpOnly,
  SameSite=Strict, Path=/api); send it back with every request. Only
  /api/health, /api/v1/openapi and /login work without it; a request
  without it gets 401 at once. Requests that change something are
  refused (403) when their Origin header names another site.

post.summary: Import units, attributes and classes from a model file (admins)
post.description:
The body is a model file (seed/model-format.md): a tree of classes with
their attributes. A class that is there already, by name, is imported
into: it gets the attributes it hasn't got, and an attribute it has must
be the same (409 otherwise). Rows below a class that gets a required
attribute are checked and given its default, as a class change does. All
or nothing; with dry_run, nothing is kept. A body that isn't a valid model
file is refused with 400.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The class to import below; the top of the class tree without it.

200.description: What it added, and what was there already.

get.summary: One class with its effective attributes

patch.summary: Rename, move or (un)mark a class as a container

delete.summary: Delete a class; with recursive=true also every class below it
delete.description:
Without `recursive`, the class must have no subclasses or items (else 409).
With `recursive=true`, the class and every class below it are deleted in one
transaction. If any of them has items, nothing is deleted (409), unless `force=true`,
which deletes the items too (with their values, stock rows and attachments).
`GET /classes/{id}/deletion` previews it.

get.summary: The class with everything below it, as a model file (admins)
get.description:
A model file (seed/model-format.md) of the class and the classes below it:
the class with all its attributes, its inherited ones as its own, and
the classes below with their own. Importing the file where the class is
changes nothing; importing it elsewhere sets up the same.

get.summary: What a recursive delete of the class would delete; deletes nothing
get.description:
Needs the same role as the delete. Unlike the delete, it reports items
without `force` instead of failing.

get.summary: Items, by name, paged by key

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Only items in this class or its subclasses.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words separated by spaces. Every word must occur, letter case ignored, as part of the item's search text: its name, the names of the classes in its path, and its text, url and choice values.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: Attribute filters, all of which must pass: a JSON list of {attribute, op, value}, the attribute by name. = takes a number, a text or true or false; >, >=, < and <= a number or a date (YYYY-MM-DD); between [low, high]; contains a text; in a list of texts. Texts ignore letter case. One passes when the item's values do, or one of its stock rows'. See api/item.md.

unit.description: What its stock is counted in, a label ("m"); null for pieces.

values.description: Values for its item attributes; the others get their class's defaults. Files are uploaded afterwards.

get.summary: One item with its values and stock rows

photo.description: null removes the photo; a photo is uploaded.

values.description: Values to set, by attribute name; null removes one. Either way it no longer follows the class's default. A file is uploaded instead.

default.description: Attributes to give their class's default, and to follow it.

patch.description: Changes the fields it has, and its values, in one transaction; refused as a whole when the values don't fit the class it is in then.

delete.summary: Delete an item (it must have no stock)
Delete a location; with recursive=true also every location below it
delete.description:
Without `recursive`, the location must have no sublocations or stock (else 409).
With `recursive=true`, the location and every location below it are deleted in one
transaction. If there is stock in any of them, nothing is deleted (409), unless
`force=true`, which deletes those stock rows too. `GET /locations/{id}/deletion`
previews it.

get.summary: What a recursive delete of the location would delete; deletes nothing
get.description:
Needs the same role as the delete. Unlike the delete, it reports stock
without `force` instead of failing.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Only this location and everything below it.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words that must each occur, letter case ignored, in the reference or the serial.

post.summary: Register stock of an item at a location

amount.description: In the item's unit; null: present, not counted.
In the item's unit; null: not counted.

photo.description: null removes the photo; a photo is uploaded.

values.description: Values to set, by attribute name; null removes one. Either way it no longer follows the class's default. A file is uploaded instead.

default.description: Attributes to give their class's default, and to follow it.

patch.description: Changes the fields it has, and its values, in one transaction. To move things, use move; a location here is for corrections.

post.summary: Move (part of) a stock row to another location
post.description: A whole row changes location and keeps its code; a part is split off into a new row with a code of its own and everything else the row has. It never merges.

amount.description: How much to move; null moves the whole row.

client.description: What the client calls itself ("WtF on Pixel 9"), for the list of sessions.

max_idle.description: Seconds the session may sit unused before it expires; null: never.

200.description:
Logged in. The session is in the cookie `wtf_session`, never in the body;
it expires after 30 days without use, and every answer renews it.

Set-Cookie.description: wtf_session=<token>; Path=/api; Max-Age=2592000; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict (and Secure over HTTPS)

429.description: Too many failed logins; one attempt per minute until a login succeeds.

204.description: Logged out; the session cookie is deleted.

put.summary: Change the own password (ends all other sessions)

end_other_sessions.description: Whether the account's other sessions end too.

password.description: Without a password the account can't log in.

patch.description: Changing the password ends the account's sessions. You can't change your own role.

password.description: null removes the password (the account can't log in).

end_sessions.description: With password, and only with it: whether the account's sessions end too. Not for one's own account.

delete.summary: Delete an account (admins; not your own)
delete.description: The account is deleted, with its sessions; its email can be used again. You can't delete your own account.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: A label code. Case and hyphens are ignored; I, L, O and U are invalid (clients map I/L to 1 and O to 0).

get.summary: What a label code belongs to

200.description: The object the code belongs to.

get.description:
A code that was handed out but that nothing has any more answers 410
(/problems/gone): what had it was deleted. A code never handed out is 404.
openapi/openapi.json, as application/json, or as application/yaml when Accept asks for YAML (JSON is valid YAML). Served without a session.
The sessions of the account the request is made with, most recently used first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session's id, as GET /me/sessions gives it.

delete.description: Another account's session is not found. The current session's id logs out, as POST /logout does, and deletes the cookie.

post.description: Every session of the account but the current one: for a lost phone.

post.summary: Merge (part of) a stock row into another row of the same item
post.description: Adds the amount (null: all of it) to the row "into", which may be at another location. Both rows must be of the same item and counted. Where they differ (reference, serial, photo, or a value), resolve must say which row's to keep for each, or the merge is refused (422, naming the differences). Merging all of it deletes the row, whose label then answers 410. Answers "into".

amount.description: How much to merge; null merges the whole row.

post.summary: Add an attribute to a class
post.description: Refused when the class has an attribute of that name, or a class below it has one of its own. A required one gets its default on every item (or stock row) below the class, and is refused without a default while there are any.

patch.summary: Change an attribute the class defines
patch.description: Fields: required, default, unit, order, and media; null removes a default, a unit or media types. Its type and scope never change. A changed default reaches every value below that follows it.

delete.summary: Remove an attribute the class defines
delete.description: From the class and the classes below it, and its values from every item (or stock row) below it.

post.summary: Rename an attribute the class defines
post.description: In the class, the classes below it, and every value below it.

post.summary: Add a choice to a choice attribute

delete.description: Refused while it is the default, or an item (or stock row) below the class has it.

post.description: In its place, in the default, and in every value below the class that has it.

put.description: It must be an image. PATCH photo null removes it.

get.summary: The file of an attachment attribute

put.summary: Upload the file of an attachment attribute
put.description: Of the media types the attribute takes, when it lists them. A patch with the value null removes it.
It must be an image. PATCH photo null removes it.

get.summary: The file of an attachment attribute

put.summary: Upload the file of an attachment attribute
put.description: Of the media types the attribute takes, when it lists them. A patch with the value null removes it.

session.name: wtf_session
session.description: The session cookie set by POST /login.

API-Revision.description: The revision of API version 1 the server implements; it grows with every addition.

Force.name: force
Force.description: With recursive: also delete what uses the deleted nodes (items of classes, stock at locations).

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: The ETag of the tree the client already has.

After.name: after
After.description: The last row of the page before (its `next`); none for the first page.

DryRun.name: dry_run
DryRun.description: Change nothing, and answer what the change would do; refused as the change would be.

file.description: The file; its Content-Type is kept (and detected when missing or application/octet-stream).

photo.description: Make it the object's photo (images only).

parent.description: Parent node; none for a root.

container.description: Holds only other classes (no items) or locations (no stock).

confirm.description: Needed for a grid of more than 1000 locations.

schema.description: grid is for locations only, and required there (null: none).

parent.description: New parent; null makes it a root.

container.description: Rejected (422) while the class has items or the location has stock.

photo.description: One of its own image attachments, or null for none.

ClassChange.description: The class, and what the change wrote.

File.description: The file; its media type is found from its first bytes.

stock.description: Number of stock rows of those items.
The live stock rows; for a deleted item, those deleted together with it.

hint.description: What to do about it, when the database knows (revision 2).

sqlstate.description: PostgreSQL error code, when the error came from the database.

next.description: With more: the `after` for the next page.

Role.description: Each role can do what the ones before it can (ACCOUNTS.md).

Values.description: Values by attribute name: a number, a text, a date (YYYY-MM-DD), true or false, a choice's text, or a file's hash. An attribute without a value is left out.

name.description: Not the name of a fixed field: id, code, name, class, unit, photo, item, location, amount, reference or serial.

container.description: Holds only other classes, no items.

attributes.description: Every attribute it has, its own and those it inherits: the item attributes, then the stock attributes, each by order.

container.description: Holds only other locations, no stock.

unit.description: What its stock is counted in, a label; null for pieces.

stock.description: Its stock rows, by location name.

item.description: Its id in an item's stock rows; the item otherwise.

amount.description: In the item's unit (whole for pieces); null: present, not counted.

id.description: The token's SHA-256, in hex; it can't be turned back into the token.

client.description: What the client called itself when logging in.

last_used.description: Written at most once a minute.

max_idle.description: Seconds it may sit unused; null: never expires.

usage.description: The last 8 addresses it was used from, newest first.

Hash.description: The SHA-256 of a file's content, as hex.

scope.description: Where its values live: on the item, or on each stock row.

unit.description: A label for the values ("mm"); nothing converts.

default.description: A value that fits; none for an attachment.

choices.description: For a choice only, and needed.

media.description: For an attachment only: the media types it takes ("application/pdf", "image/*").

order.description: Its place on screen among the attributes of its scope.

Defaulted.description: The names of the values that follow the class's default.

items.description: How many items it wrote (or would have).

stock.description: How many stock rows it wrote (or would have).
